links.outcome: Safety scores of LLM responses to red-flag migraine questions (possible stroke or secondary headache)
links.effect: Among 25 red-flag questions, both models had high safety scores; no significant difference in safety after correction (overall safety adjusted p = 0.075).
links.quote: Among 25 red-flag questions, both models had high safety scores; only readability remained significantly different after correction.

links.outcome: Readability (Ateşman score) of LLM answers to patient-facing migraine questions
links.effect: Ateşman readability was 74.75 ± 17.43 for DeepSeek-V3 vs 60.70 ± 19.97 for GPT-4o (adjusted p < 0.001); GPT-4o answers were harder to read.
links.quote: DeepSeek-V3 had higher accuracy scores than GPT-4o (4.54 ± 0.49 vs 4.37 ± 0.50; Holm-adjusted p = 0.026), higher completeness scores (3.98 ± 0.44 vs 3.46 ± 0.61; adjusted p < 0.001), and higher Ateşman readability scores (74.75 ± 17.43 vs 60.70 ± 19.97; adjusted p < 0.001).

screen.reason: Evaluates and compares the accuracy, completeness, empathy, readability, and safety of GPT-4o and DeepSeek-V3 on patient-facing migraine questions without evaluating a specific deployment practice or safeguard intervention.
